scope: Five existing procedure proposals only. No inventory, defect, status, runtime result, account, browser state, system permission, or history data was changed or exercised.

fixture.purpose: Owned synthetic deterministic download source. For each role independently, open the HTML fixture in that role's dedicated disposable Chrome profile, click its download link, and verify the completed filename before that role's case. No file contents contain user data.
fixture.execution_state: Source fixture created; neither role profile, browser fixture, nor download was run. Completed-download and cleanup outcomes remain runtime-unverified.
fixture.cleanup: For each role, record the exact downloaded file path if the owned fixture is downloaded. After that role's sanitized evidence capture, close Chrome, remove only that known owned downloaded file by its recorded path, verify it is absent, then retire/delete that role's dedicated disposable profile. If the path or absence cannot be confirmed, report downloaded-file cleanup unverified; profile deletion alone does not prove file deletion. No cleanup was executed in this source-only proposal.

coverage_boundary.permission_negative: Explicitly not applicable/unreachable via manual Catalog Run, which bypasses dispatcher auth. Do not use an invented toggle or permission removal. A separate dispatcher/agent denial procedure is still required.

EXT-F-4042-T01.title: List recent controlled history entries
preconditions: For this role, complete the shared receipt-bound setup in its own dedicated disposable Chrome profile and prepare this role's fixtures; repeat independently in a different profile for the other role.
Complete shared history fixture preparation in the disposable profile; the two fixture visits must be within the selected lookback window.

Select All handlers in the Tools Catalog surface selector so the internal list_recent_history delegate is visible. The manual runner directly invokes this handler; this procedure does not establish dispatcher permission behavior.
steps: Warm run: open list_recent_history and run with {"minutes":60,"max_results":50} immediately after the controlled fixture visits.

Inspect the inline result's count and items. Find only the two recorded fixture URLs and compare their titles, visit timestamps, and visit counts with the browser actions; do not copy other result rows into evidence.
Run the same arguments once more and confirm the fixture entries remain present and ordered newest first by last_visit_ms.

With the same Tools row selected, run {"minutes":0,"max_results":50}; expect argument validation rejection before execution because minutes must be a positive integer (maximum 43,200). Do not interpret an empty result as the negative assertion.
After the required extension/panel/target-tab reload, rerun the same arguments and compare only the controlled fixture entries.

After this role's sanitized fixture assertion, close Chrome for this role; remove only its recorded owned downloaded file if one was created and verify absence, then retire/delete this role's disposable profile. If file path or absence cannot be confirmed, report downloaded-file cleanup unverified. Repeat the complete setup, fixture, run, and cleanup lifecycle independently for the other role. Preserve only sanitized build/run receipt and the specific assertion result.
expected: The result has a count and items array; controlled pages visited within 60 minutes appear with their URL/title and visit metadata, subject to Chrome history API results.

Items are ordered by descending last_visit_ms when timestamps are present. Exact total count and visit_count may include browser-generated changes, so use the two known fixture URLs as the assertion boundary.
An unavailable API or surfaced error is recorded as unverified/failure evidence for review; an empty list does not prove the feature works when fixture visits are missing.

shared_role_lifecycle.setup: Use separate dedicated disposable Chrome profiles for member and admin. In each profile independently load the exact receipt-bound extension build, sign in as that role, prepare only that profile's controlled history and recently-closed fixtures, and perform the synthetic download in that profile before its download case. Record fixture URLs, tab session ID, downloaded filename and exact owned file path locally for that role; do not reuse a profile, fixture result, session ID, or download record across roles.
shared_role_lifecycle.execution: Run each proposed Catalog case separately as member and admin, including warm, malformed-schema and required reload steps against that role's own fixtures. Label evidence by role and loaded build receipt. Catalog output only proves direct local handler behavior when observed; it does not prove account authorization, dispatcher Ask/Act denial, or live advertised agent binding.
shared_role_lifecycle.cleanup: After each role's cases and sanitized evidence capture, close that role's Chrome profile. Remove and verify absence of only its recorded owned downloaded file, then retire/delete that role's disposable profile. Record either verified cleanup or explicitly unverified downloaded-file cleanup. Do not infer that deleting a profile removes a file Chrome saved elsewhere.
